dns_records_extra.query_failed: All CAA, SRV and TLSA queries on {domain} failed
finding.dns_records_extra.caa_missing: No CAA record: any certificate authority may issue a certificate for this domain. Publish a CAA record that limits the authorised issuers.
module.dns_records_extra.checks: Reads CAA records (authorised certificate authorities, climbing to the organisational domain), SRV records (common services: SIP, mail, directory…) and TLSA records (DANE on port 443 and the mail servers).
module.dns_records_extra.fix:
Before writing a CAA record, list the certificate authorities that actually issue your certificates (module "Public certificates (Certificate Transparency)" or the issuer shown in the browser): a CAA that leaves one out will block its next renewal.
In the domain's DNS zone (DNS host or registrar), add one CAA record of type `issue` per authorized authority; the value is the authority's domain name, for example `letsencrypt.org`, `digicert.com`, `sectigo.com` or `pki.goog`.
If you use no wildcard certificate (`*.example.com`), add `0 issuewild ";"` to forbid them; otherwise, name the authorized authority in an `issuewild` record.
Optional: add an `iodef` record with a contact address (`0 iodef "mailto:security@example.com"`); few authorities act on it, but it costs nothing. A CAA set on the main domain also applies to its subdomains, unless they have their own CAA.
For each SRV record found (SIP telephony, XMPP, LDAP, Kerberos, mail...): check that the service must be announced publicly; otherwise delete the record and close the matching port.
Only publish a TLSA record (DANE) if the domain is signed with DNSSEC, and update it before every certificate or key change: a stale TLSA makes clients that check DANE reject the service.
Check with `dig +short CAA example.com`, then test issuing or renewing a certificate with the authorized authority to make sure nothing is blocked.
module.dns_records_extra.fix_snippet:
# DNS
example.com.  3600 IN CAA 0 issue "letsencrypt.org"
example.com.  3600 IN CAA 0 issuewild ";"
example.com.  3600 IN CAA 0 iodef "mailto:security@example.com"

# Bash
dig +short CAA example.com
module.dns_records_extra.title: Additional DNS records (CAA, SRV, TLSA)
module.dns_records_extra.why: A CAA record limits which authorities may issue a certificate for the domain; DANE binds the expected certificate to DNS; SRV records reveal side services (telephony, instant messaging) that standard probes miss.
